headline: South Asia: Pakistan rejects Afghan Taliban's claims of civilian casualties in counterterrorism operations
script:
Good evening. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistan rejects Afghan Taliban's claims of civilian casualties in counterterrorism operations.
- Western Russia: Two killed in Russian strikes on Kharkiv.
- Africa: Sudan experiences massive power outages after RSF drone strikes.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Pentagon cautions personnel against betting using insider information.
- Military Times, 7 hours ago: Pentagon cautions personnel against betting using insider information.
Hostile foreign intelligence services can track bets made by U.S. military personnel on prediction markets to anticipate American movements, targets and timing, Hegseth warned.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.
The Caribbean: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Pope Leo XIV confirms trip to Argentina following lung surgery.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 9 hours ago: Pope Leo XIV confirms trip to Argentina following lung surgery.
‘I look forward to returning to the continent,’ the pontiff said. He will also visit Uruguay and Peru La entrada Pope Leo XIV confirms trip to Argentina following lung surgery se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Two killed in Russian strikes on Kharkiv.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Two killed in Russian strikes on Kharkiv.
The attack hit Kharkiv’s Novobavarskyi district, damaging apartment buildings, houses and cars. A 17-year-old girl was among those injured.
- The Moscow Times, 13 hours ago: ‘Still Just a Child’: The Russian Teenagers Fighting and Dying in Ukraine.
A growing number of Russian soldiers who were still schoolchildren when the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began are being killed in the war.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 9 hours ago: At least seven hits: OSINT analysts' photos show consequences of missile strike on Russian military plant.
Photos show damage to the Energiya plant, Russia’s sole producer of batteries for aerial bomb guidance systems. An OSINT analyst says two key buildings were hit, one destroyed and the other gutted by fire.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 12 hours ago: One killed and two children injured in Russian drone attack on Pavlohrad.
One person was killed when Russian forces attacked the city of Pavlohrad in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast with a drone on Monday 26 October.
Southern Europe - bottom line: European defense ministers warn Putin isn’t looking for peace.
- Politico Europe, 6 hours ago: European defense ministers warn Putin isn’t looking for peace.
The EU's top diplomat Kaja Kallas said she expects a "brutal" winter ahead for Ukraine.
- Politico Europe, 9 hours ago: Europe is living in a new ‘era of darkness,’ Finland’s Stubb warns.
The Finnish president says Europe needs new security structures to keep peace in this “a dog-eat-dog world.”
- Balkan Insight, 16 hours ago: European Leaders Welcome Victory for Serbia’s Opposition Student List.
European officials and leaders from Balkan states congratulated the Student List on its election victory, expressing hopes for democratic changes that will accelerate Serbia’s progress towards EU membership.
- Balkan Insight, 18 hours ago: ‘Real Grave’: Kosovo Seeks to Correct Mistakes Made in Identifying War Dead.
In trying to identify the remains of more than 300 war dead, authorities in Kosovo are revisiting those identified and buried shortly after the end of hostilities and without the help of DNA, searching for possible mistakes.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Sudan experiences massive power outages after RSF drone strikes.
- Africanews, 10 hours ago: Sudan experiences massive power outages after RSF drone strikes.
Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces launched a coordinated drone attack Monday against five power stations, causing mass power outages across the country's east, a government official told AFP.
- Africanews, 8 hours ago: Russia: flames engulf buildings after Ukrainian drone attack in Voronezh region.
At least two people were killed and 17 injured in a Ukrainian drone attack on Russia's Voronezh region. Flames engulfed buildings, while falling debris struck a commuter train.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 11 hours ago: Ethiopia: At Least 48 Civilians Killed in Weekend Attacks in Ethiopia's Oromia Region, Once Again.
[Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- At least 48 people have been killed and more than 31 others wounded, some severely, in attacks by armed men in Chole and Birbo kebeles of Shirka Woreda, Arsi Zone, in southeastern Oromia, residents who attended the victims' mass funeral told Addis Standard, describing door-to-door killings, looting and the use of heavy weapons.
- Africanews, 11 hours ago: Nurse killed, health worker injured in DR Congo Ebola attack.
A nurse was killed and a health worker severely injured after being attacked while responding to an Ebola alert in Congo, according to the World Health Organisation.
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Jordan strikes Syria after church attack, killing at least seven people.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: Jordan strikes Syria after church attack, killing at least seven people.
Syria closes border crossings with Jordan after air strikes kill seven people in Deraa and Suweyda, including children.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, just now: England’s Harry Kane wins Ballon d’Or, Alexia Putellas takes women’s award.
Bayern Munich striker becomes the first Englishman to win the prestigious award in 25 years, after Michael Owen in 2001.
- Jerusalem Post, 10 hours ago: IDF stops short of denying report Zamir, Netanyahu clashed over Iran strike before elections.
"The operational activities and factors considered by the IDF are based solely on security, professional, substantive, and nonpartisan considerations," the military said.
- Jerusalem Post, one hour ago: England, Bayern forward Kane crowned 2026 Ballon d'Or winner.
Kane is the first Englishman to win the prestigious award in 25 years, after Michael Owen won it in 2001.
South Africa - bottom line: South Africa: How to Thaw a Health System Frozen in Fear.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 16 hours ago: South Africa: How to Thaw a Health System Frozen in Fear.
[spotlight] South Africa's public healthcare system finds itself caught between two incomplete revolutions - the democratic dream of a decentralised District Health System, and the march toward National Health Insurance. Health systems experts argue that structural changes won't save a system that is scared stiff. The most urgent task facing the system, they say, is to help frontline doctors and nurses reimagine what is possible.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 13 hours ago: South Africa: President Ramaphosa Congratulates Brazilian President On Re-Election.
[SAnews.gov.za] President Cyril Ramaphosa has, on behalf of the government and people of South Africa, extended his warm congratulations and well wishes to Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on his re-election for a historic fourth term.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 14 hours ago: Namibia: Etango Mine Targets 2028 First Uranium Production.
[Namibian] The Etango open-pit uranium mine is targeting commissioning and first yellowcake production towards the end of 2028.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 15 hours ago: Malawi: Video Fuels Questions Over Chaponda Link to Church Chaos.
[Nyasa Times] A political storm has erupted after video footage circulating on social media allegedly showed a member of Foreign Affairs Minister George Chaponda's security detail among a group accused of attacking vehicles linked to former president Lazarus Chakwera and intimidating journalists during the CCAP Blantyre Synod's 150th anniversary celebrations.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan rejects Afghan Taliban's claims of civilian casualties in counterterrorism operations.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 15 hours ago: Pakistan rejects Afghan Taliban's claims of civilian casualties in counterterrorism operations.
The Foreign Office (FO) on Monday rejected allegations made by the Afghan Taliban government regarding civilian casualties in Islamabad’s counterterrorism campaign in the neighbouring country, maintaining that Pakistan’s conduct always “reflected restraint” and the response was “proportionate to the level of threat”. The Afghan Taliban have repeatedly claimed civilian casualties in Pakistani strikes in Afghanistan; Pakistani authorities have denied the accusations, holding that they target military and terrorist infrastructure.
- Dawn (Pakistan), South China Morning Post - China, Al Jazeera - Middle East, The Hindu - International, 6 hours ago: Jordan arrests 3 in dawn raid over church attack.
Jordanian security forces on Monday arrested three suspects over an attack on a church last week that killed nine people, with the trio wounded in a dawn raid and shootout, authorities said. The kingdom’s Public Security Directorate said the group were apprehended at an abandoned house where they had barricaded themselves inside and opened fire on security forces. One of the suspects was taken to hospital in critical condition, while the other two were stable, Jordan’s state broadcaster Al-Mamlaka reported. There were no casualties among security forces, it added.
- The Hindu - International, 15 hours ago: Intercepted missile after Houthis hit Riyadh airport, says Saudi coalition.
The Houthis have carried out waves of strikes on the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, including an attack this month that killed 13 people and injured more than 300
- Dawn (Pakistan), 16 hours ago: Pakistan condemns Houthi attacks targeting Makkah, Madina as 'grave violation' of Saudi sovereignty.
Pakistan on Monday condemned Houthi missile attacks targeting Saudi Arabia’s Makkah and Madina regions, terming them a “grave violation” of the kingdom’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. According to a statement issued by the Foreign Office (FO), these “reprehensible attacks constitute a grave violation of Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity and demonstrate a blatant disregard for the sanctity of Islam’s holiest sites and the safety of civilians”. Pakistan reiterated its “unwavering solidarity” with Saudi Arabia and its firm commitment to the Makkah Alliance, the FO said.

- South China Morning Post - China, just now: Australia to host USS Colorado as first US nuclear submarine under Aukus pact.
The Pentagon has assigned the USS Colorado as the first US nuclear-powered attack submarine to join a rotating force to be based in Western Australia. The 115-metre (380-foot) Virginia-class submarine, armed with land-attack missiles and sophisticated torpedoes, would sail to the new Australian base in late 2027, officials said on Tuesday. The deployment was a “significant milestone” in building up a joint US-Australia-UK deterrence in the Pacific under their Aukus defence pact, the allies said...

Brown, 37, was given an eight-month suspended sentence at London’s Southwark Crown Court ‌after he admitted a charge of affray over the attack on Abraham Diaw at the Tape nightclub in February 2023. Taiwan is developing an AI-powered system to coordinate drone fleets for maritime surveillance and countering “grey-zone” activities, with researchers completing a simulation involving 20 aircraft, according to the island’s Ocean Affairs Council. The system, which is funded by the council, would allow different types of drones to autonomously divide tasks, plan routes and coordinate their movements while providing wide-area, persistent surveillance for coastguard operations. India - bottom line: Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or, becomes 1st player to claim two awards in one night.
- Times of India - Top Stories, Buenos Aires Herald, 2 hours ago: Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or, becomes 1st player to claim two awards in one night.
Harry Kane made history at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony, becoming the first Englishman in 25 years to win football’s most prestigious individual honour. The Bayern Munich striker also claimed the Gerd Müller Trophy, completing a historic double after scoring 73 goals for club and country. His extraordinary campaign marks a defining moment in his career and English football history.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 8 hours ago: ‘Diabolical regime’: Ex-US general warns Iran rebuilding nuclear programme.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: Delaware sank 180-foot ship bought for $1 to create artificial reef.
In a strategic move to enhance marine ecosystems, the retired fishing vessel F/V Calcasieu Pass has been sunk off the Delaware coast to function as an artificial reef. This initiative, aimed at supporting diverse aquatic species, involved meticulously clearing hazardous materials before the sinking. Environmental authorities will oversee the area, monitoring the growth and health of the marine habitats it spawns in the years to come.

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Magnitude-4.9 earthquake strikes off South Australia coast.
- ABC News Australia, 4 hours ago: Magnitude-4.9 earthquake strikes off South Australia coast.
Residents around Adelaide have reported feeling an earthquake this morning, with Geoscience Australia saying the epicentre was about 100 kilometres offshore, between Kangaroo Island and the south-east coast.
- The Guardian - Australia, 6 hours ago: Morning Mail: Endangered turtles ‘at risk’ from gas drilling; Jacinda Ardern’s Sydney job; and Star Trek actor dies.
Want to get this in your inbox every weekday? Sign up for the Morning Mail here, and finish your day with our Politics, really newsletter. Morning everyone. Our exclusive top story reveals that the environment watchdog has warned about the threat to coral and wildlife posed by Woodside’s plan to develop a gasfield off the Western Australian coast – piling pressure on state and federal ministers to reject the project.
- The Guardian - Australia, 3 hours ago: The chaos in France is a ‘warning signal’ for Australia’s public spending and rising costs.
Australia’s public debt may be well below that of France but there are lessons to be taken from its economic woes Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast The explosion of discontent that led to major protests and violence in France and across Europe is a “warning signal” that Australia could follow the same path without an “honest conversation” about the budget, economists say.
- The Guardian - Australia, 19 hours ago: Angus Taylor criticised for ‘tone deaf’ response to alleged attack on Helen Haines.
Zali Steggall and Monique Ryan say Coalition leader was wrong to deny link between parliamentary debate and political violence Angus Taylor has been criticised for his response to the alleged attack on Helen Haines, with crossbenchers Monique Ryan and Zali Steggall labelling a speech by the opposition leader “tone deaf” and saying he did not “read the room”. Parliament returned in Canberra on Monday, a week after an alleged attack outside the Indi MP’s northern Victorian electorate office, which led to her losing both legs.
